theInterimFinding.what: The live layer publishes an INTERIM family with a leading `I-` qualifier (14 values, 1,229 polygons, 5.5% of the layer). The parser in this branch leaves every one of them unrecognised, so the stamp writes the published value verbatim and the router's mapDistrict declines it (normalizeCode('I-SF-2') = 'ISF2' matches no row and no guarded prefix). These are parcels whose PREVIOUS reading was a resolvable district.
theInterimFinding.whyThisIsTheCheckpointsHeadline: CP1 pre-registered exactly this outcome (falsifier 2's band names I-SF-2) and this lane therefore ships it; what CP1 could not see is the SIZE and the fact that the previous source published the base code for the same parcels. Both are now measured.

evidenceThatThePreviousReadingServedThes: The census records NO interim value anywhere: 0 of its 70 Austin rows carry an `I-` prefix, while it records the base code for exactly the parcels the dry run finds under `I-`: Hays RR 270 vs I-RR 272 (+0.7%), Hays SF-2 88 vs I-SF-2 89 (+1.1%), Williamson SF-2 5946 vs I-SF-2 5129 (-13.7%), Williamson MF-2 347 vs I-MF-2 245 (-29%). The Hays pairs are the tightest because Hays' two instruments agree to 0.9% at account grain; Williamson agrees to 0.0002%.

The old layer cannot be re-read to settle it: Publish_Zoning_AGOL now answers ArcGIS error 499 'Token Required' even for ?f=json (measured in this lane), so the previous vintage is no longer publicly readable.
evidenceOnWhatTheInterimDistrictMEANS: City of Austin ordinance amendment review sheet C2O-2009-017 (services.austintexas.gov/edims/document.cfm?id=132373): interim zoning is the designation granted on annexation until permanent zoning is established; I-SF-2 is 'Interim Single Family Residence Standard Lot'; the sheet's own rationale is that the amendment lets owners build 'following the same regulations used throughout the city in single-family neighborhoods with standard-sized lots'.

Austin development-standards table, 20160616-041 agenda late backup (edims?id=256732): I-SF-2 = min lot 5,750 sq ft, min width 50 ft, max building coverage 40%, max impervious cover 45%, height 35 ft, setbacks street front 25 ft / street side 15 ft / interior side 5 ft / rear 10 ft.

The shipped austin-tx.json SF-2 row (read at source, not edited): front_ft 25, rear_ft 10, side_ft 5, max_height_ft 35 — the same setback triple the ordinance table gives I-SF-2. So for SF-2 the interim base carries the same setback numbers, and declining it is a false absence (P-255's own defect class), not a conservative miss.

The layer's OTHER field does NOT provide this mapping: ZONING_BASE for the interim polygons is the family only — I-SF-2 -> 'SF' (662 polygons), I-SF-4A -> 'SF' (220), I-MF-2 -> 'MF' (1), while I-RR -> 'RR' (321) and I-GR -> 'GR' (2) happen to be complete. So A-164's 'ZONING_BASE collapses codes' is confirmed on the interim family too, and neither field names the interim base.
theInterimFinding.whatTheLaneDeliberatelyDidNotDo: It did not enable an interim rule, and did not touch austin-tx.json. CP1 pre-registered the interim family as unrecognised and the dispatch's parser spec is explicit ('returns an explicit unrecognised base ... when no known base prefixes the value'), and the dispatch forbids changing the setback table. Moving the pre-registered band after seeing the measurement is the failure mode pre-registration exists to prevent.
theInterimFinding.theRulingThisLeaves: Either (a) the parser gains a declared leading-qualifier rule (`interimQualifiers: ['I']`) so `I-<X>` parses to base `<X>` with an interim disclosure carried in the parse result, or (b) austin-tx.json gains interim rows for the I-* family. (a) is a one-line registry change plus a test over the 14 live values; (b) is P-258's table. Either way the census re-run is what grades it: unresolved, the ~6.4K parcels that the census recorded as SERVED districts in Hays+Williamson (and the Travis family at feature grain) become district-misses, so Austin's district misses would RISE rather than fall.
theInterimFinding.pairedControl: The layer's own group-by says the interim family is 1,229 polygons of 22,502 named-code polygons (5.46%); the dry run's parcel counts independently put 23,499 of 256,008 Austin-polygon parcels in that family across the three counties. Two instruments, different grains, same family — the family is not an artifact of one parser path.

fleetMemoryScratch.text: On this Windows box PowerShell's `*>` / `>` redirection writes UTF-16LE. A log read with readFileSync(path,'utf8') is NUL-interleaved and every regex silently misses (`could not read parcels read` on a line that is visibly present). Detect the FF FE BOM and decode utf16le, or write logs with a Node writer. Cost this lane ~10 minutes of a phantom parsing bug.

`heavy-scan-lease.mjs` looks a lease up BY TOKEN: if you do not persist holderToken at take time, `renew`/`release` answer LEASE_LOST (409) because `list` prints the id, not the token. Persist id+token+expiry in your scratch the moment you take it.

Comparing `zoning-stamp`'s `parcels read` with the P-255 census's per-county `parcels` as if both were parcels: they are different denominations (feature vs account) and in Travis differ by 2.18x. Do not re-attempt this comparison without first converting to accounts (SELECT count(DISTINCT prop_id)).
